title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the 'motivic Galois group' (1965). At the top, a passage is struck out with diagonal lines and marked '??' in the margin. It asked whether, for non-constant motives, knowing the operations Θ_X (derivations acting via connections) on the realizations V_C (V ∈ Ob M) determines the 'structure elements 1° and 2°' introduced earlier. That question is abandoned.

The new section is titled in the margin 'intrinsic interpretation of the datum of an integrable connection on a fibre functor'. Its content, in modern terms:

1. Let M be a ⊗-category over k_0 with a fibre functor with values in k_0, i.e. a neutral Tannakian category. Then M ≅ Rep_{k_0}(G), with G the affine group scheme of ⊗-automorphisms of the fibre functor.
2. Let K/k_0 be a field extension and F_K = F ⊗_{k_0} K. Problem: classify the ways of putting on each V_K = V ⊗_{k_0} K an integrable connection relative to K/k_0, i.e. an action of Der(K/k_0). The connection must be natural in V and compatible with ⊗.
3. Since each V has a k_0-structure, there is a canonical (trivial) connection Θ_0 = 1 ⊗ d.
4. Any other connection differs by a K-linear map ω^V : Der(K/k_0) → End(V)_K, with Θ^V_X = Θ_0{}^V_X + ω^V(X).
5. Naturality in V and compatibility with ⊗ (Leibniz rule ω^{V⊗W} = ω^V⊗1 + 1⊗ω^W, unit trivial) say exactly that, for each X, the family (ω^V(X))_V is a ⊗-derivation of F_K. Hence it is an element ω(X) ∈ Lie(G_K) = 𝔤 ⊗ K.
6. So the datum is a K-linear ω : Der(K/k_0) → 𝔤_K, i.e. a 𝔤-valued 1-form.
7. On the next page, integrability becomes the Maurer–Cartan / zero-curvature equation Θ_{0X}ω(Y) − Θ_{0Y}ω(X) = ω([X,Y]) − [ω(X),ω(Y)].
8. Grothendieck then notes that ω usually comes from a finitely generated subfield k, as ω_k ∈ Ω^1_{k/k_0} ⊗ 𝔤. Equivalently it is a map 𝔤^∨ → Ω^1_{k/k_0}. He then turns to the question of when morphisms u : V_K → W_K commuting with the Θ_X are k_0-rational, invoking Gauss–Manin in characteristic 0.

Purpose: understand how the motivic Galois group over a non-constant base, or over a field K transcendental over k_0, relates to the constant one through the Gauss–Manin connection. This is a Tannakian treatment of 'connections on a fibre functor', i.e. flat G-connections on the trivial G-torsor over Spec K.
errors: No substantive error. Implicit assumptions: the fibre functor is neutral (values in k_0), and naturality of ω^V means commuting with all morphisms of M. Both are needed for identifying ⊗-derivations of F_K with Lie(G)⊗K.

Gauge equivalence is not addressed: changing the trivialization by g ∈ G(K) transforms ω by Ad(g)ω + g^*θ_MC. Isomorphism classes of ⊗-connections are therefore not simply the flat forms ω. Grothendieck may intend the fixed k_0-structure to rigidify, but this is not stated.

On the next page, the left-hand side of the integrability condition is labelled dω(X∧Y). With the standard convention, dω(X,Y) also contains −ω([X,Y]), which he places on the right. The formula itself is consistent; the label is slightly loose.

ideas.what: ⊗-compatible natural connections on F⊗K for a neutral Tannakian category correspond to K-linear maps Der(K/k_0) → Lie(G)⊗K, via ⊗-derivations of the fibre functor = Lie algebra of G
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of G-connections / connection 1-forms with values in Lie(G); Lie(G) = ⊗-derivations of the fibre functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972, Catégories tannakiennes, Lie algebra via derivations); Deligne (1990); Katz (1987) for differential Galois groups

ideas.what: Integrability of the ⊗-connection is equivalent to the Maurer–Cartan (flatness) equation for ω
ideas.modern_name: zero-curvature / Maurer–Cartan equation for a flat G-connection

ideas.what: Using Gauss–Manin on realizations of non-constant motives to compare the motivic Galois group over K with the constant one, and to test k_0-rationality of horizontal morphisms
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection and motivic Galois groups in families; theorem of the fixed part; differential Galois group vs. monodromy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971; theorem of the fixed part); Katz; Y. André (1992 Compositio, Mumford–Tate groups and the fixed part)

missed.claim: Already in 1965, Grothendieck frames integrable connections compatible with ⊗ on a fibre functor as Lie(G)-valued flat 1-forms. This explicitly links the motivic Galois group with differential (Picard–Vessiot-type) Galois theory via Gauss–Manin, an approach later realized by Katz (1987), Deligne (1990) and André. It is an early, unpublished Tannakian formulation rather than a new result.
missed.quote: Interprétation intrinsèque de la donnée d'une connexion intégrable sur foncteur fibre ... est une "dérivation" du foncteur fibre F_K, donc défini par un élément de 𝔤_K, où 𝔤 = Lie G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: it documents that the Tannakian/differential-Galois link to motives was part of Grothendieck's 1965 programme. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, clean and early (1965) Tannakian treatment of connections on a fibre functor, tied to motives and Gauss–Manin. The content itself is standard today (Saavedra, Deligne, Katz, André), so it is interesting historically but not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: First line: '(rationnels [?] pas nécessairement constants)' is more likely '(motifs pas nécessairement constants)'.
The struck-out top paragraph is cancelled by diagonal strokes. The margin has '??' next to a crossed-out word (possibly 'oui').
Margin box reads approximately: 'Interprétation intrinsèque de la donnée d'une connexion intégrable sur un foncteur fibre' (the last words are partly crossed out).
'connexion intégrable rel. à K/k_0' is an interlinear insertion; 'fonctorielle' is struck out and the line continues 'en V, et "compatible avec ⊗"'.
In the definition of ω^V, the target is End(V)_K. The struck-out word after it looks like 'K-dérivation' rather than 'K-linéaire'.
'pas défini par un élément de [-Lie-] 𝔤_K' is the correct reading: 'Lie' is struck before 𝔤_K.
